subject: Re: Pilot ops alignment, timetable & risk matrix
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightframe.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-03-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ops alignment, proposed timetable & success criteria

Hi Ellen / Brad —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have a shared plan to kick off the pilot next month. TL;DR: Redwood can run a 4-week evaluation (staging + live pilot) focused on latency, cost-per-token, and end-to-end inference correctness; below are proposed acceptance gates, owners, and an initial risk matrix.

Proposed high-level timeline
- Week 0 (Mar 13–19): Kickoff, NDA/MSA signature, environment access (SFTP/sample data, network allowlist).
- Week 1 (Mar 20–26): Baseline runs on sample dataset; measure latency/cost; integrate prefix caching.
- Week 2 (Mar 27–Apr 2): Feature testing (streaming, function-calls), security review; run preliminary eval prompts.
- Week 3 (Apr 3–9): Stability and load tests; customer acceptance testing (CAT) for 3 key flows.
- Week 4 (Apr 10–16): Final acceptance and handoff recommendations.

Success criteria (customer to confirm):
- P1: Median 95th-percentile latency < 350ms for the main completion flow on 8k tokens.
- P2: End-to-end accuracy — top-1 fidelity >= 88% against curated evaluation set.
- P3: Token unit cost delta <= 20% vs current baseline with equivalent throughput.
- P4: No unresolved Sev-1 blocking bugs at handoff; documented mitigations for Sev-2.

Owners / Roles
- Redwood Sales (me): Jordan — procurement, timeline, executive updates.
- Redwood CS: Marissa — runbook, onboarding, eval prompts, QA triage.
- Redwood SRE: Sean — infra/network, escalation, monitoring hooks.
- BrightFrame: Ellen (technical lead), Brad (product owner), Procurement contact TBD.

Initial top risks and proposed mitigations (we'll expand into a tracker):
1) Data access delays (customer-side) — Mitigation: allow stubbed sample data; Marissa will run synthetic tests until access is granted.
2) Model regression on specific prompts — Mitigation: staged acceptance gates + automated regression alerts; fallback to smaller model variant if production SLOs are violated.
3) Network egress issues with VPC — Mitigation: Sean to provide a minimal allowlist and we can use temporary VPN tunnel for validation.

Attachments: redwood_poc_runbook_v1.docx (live doc with runbook checklist).

Ask: Can you confirm the success criteria above and whether procurement (procurement@brightframe.com) should be looped now? If Mar 13 kickoff works, we'll send the MSA link and runbook updates by Monday.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Ellen —

Great to meet you briefly on the call. Per Jordan's timeline and your maintenance window, shifting the baseline start to Mar 21 works fine. I attached the current POC templates and network requirements we commonly use (pf_poc_template.xlsx, network_requirements.pdf).

Quick operational checklist I'm going to own:
- Runbook and evaluation prompts — I'll publish a curated prompt set (3 flows, ~40 prompts) by Mar 8.
- Sample data — please share a 1–5k row CSV or an SFTP endpoint for pseudonymized samples by Mar 10. If you can't share data, we will run against synthetic data with clear caveats.
- Monitoring hooks — we'll provide a lightweight Prometheus endpoint and a request-id header to help trace requests; Sean will own the onboarding for allowlist/IPs.

I also added a short acceptance gating plan:
- Gate A (baseline): sanity + latency check on sample set (>50 runs). Owner: Marissa.
- Gate B (feature): streaming/ function-call correctness. Owner: BrightFrame (Ellen).
- Gate C (stress): stability under 2x expected concurrency. Owner: Sean.

Attachments: pf_poc_template.xlsx (POC checklist + customer input sheet), network_requirements.pdf.

I'll publish the shared Drive folder with the runbook and prompts tomorrow: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-POC-Runbook-BF

Best,
Marissa

Ellen / Procurement team —

We just uploaded the DocuSign MSA link for the evaluation (https://www.docusign.net/link/MSA-BrightFrame-8392). Jordan from my side will track signature progress and we can start provisioning once signed. Procurement, please let me know if you need any deviation notes.

A quick note on the risk matrix we plan to track in the runbook (I'll paste an excerpt here):
- Risk: Sample data delays — Impact: schedule slip (1–2 weeks) — Mitigation: run synthetic suite + parallel item owner: Marissa — Escalation: Jordan (sales) then Head of CS.
- Risk: Latency regression with long contexts — Impact: customer-facing degradation — Mitigation: enable KV prefix caching + model variant fallback; run targeted latency benches — Escalation: Sean (SRE) -> Eng lead.
- Risk: Security evidence request (SOC2) — Impact: procurement hold — Mitigation: provide SOC2 artifacts and a brief security Q&A; if additional attestation needed, Redwood will propose a scoped SOC attestation engagement — Escalation: Jordan -> Security + Legal.

If a blocking bug shows up during Gate B (feature correctness) that we cannot mitigate within 48 hours, the automatic fallback will be to route traffic to a verified model variant and schedule an incident triage. That keeps your customer flows live while we remediate.

I'll also ask Sean to open a Zendesk ticket so we have formal tracking for Sev events.

Jordan
